Hey Dylan,

We started seeing significant latency and intermittent stalls on the streaming chat endpoint from about 08:55 AM EST. Users report long gaps (3–10s) between partial responses, and in some sessions the stream stops entirely after ~45 tokens. This is impacting our live support product for a handful of accounts.

Example session ID: 3f8b-quick-1123 — attached a short trace (session_trace_1123.txt). We are on the us-east-1 region and using the streaming endpoint with max_tokens=1024, temperature=0.0.

Can you confirm if this is on your side and what mitigations you recommend right now? We need something we can push quickly to reduce customer impact.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
VP Engineering, QuickServe
liam@quickserve.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@quickserve.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-08T09:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: QuickServe | High latency affecting streaming chat sessions

Hi Liam — thanks for the trace and the clear examples. We're seeing correlated token pacing anomalies in the us-east shard that correspond with the timestamps you provided.

Immediate steps I recommend you try while we triage on our side:
- Switch to non-streaming (single-response) for the most latency-sensitive endpoints as a temporary fallback (reduces partial-chunk waiting).
- Reduce max_tokens to 256 for interactive flows where possible to shorten response windows.
- Add a client-side short-timeout + exponential backoff (250ms initial, 2x) when a chunk gap exceeds 2s; retry the request to a fresh connection.
- If you rely on streaming for partial UI updates, use a parallel polling path that checks for completed results every 500–750ms as a bridge.

I've attached a short config snippet (quickserve_temp_configs.md) with recommended temp settings you can flip today. We're continuing to investigate the root cause; Monica is pulled in for ops coordination. I'll follow up with a post-incident summary and proposed credit for the impact window.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll move quickly.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com

Attachment: quickserve_temp_configs.md (text)

Subject: Post-incident summary: QuickServe streaming latency (Nov 8)

Hi Liam —

Thank you again for the prompt report and for attaching the trace; it was very helpful. Below is a short summary of what we found, the mitigations we applied, and recommended actions on your side.

1) What happened
- Between ~08:55 and ~10:25 EST on 2025-11-08 we experienced token-pacing variance on a subset of us-east streaming nodes. The variance caused gaps between streaming chunks (median gap during the window: ~2.8s; 95th percentile ~9.2s) and in a small percentage of sessions the stream dropped after the KV cache handoff.

2) Root cause (summary)- A combination of an inefficient kernel path triggered by a sudden traffic pattern change and a KV cache eviction race caused increased CPU wait and token emission jitter on affected nodes. A background kernel patch (deployed ~10:20) corrected the inefficient path and we ran a targeted rebalance across the pool.

3) What we did
- Deployed a kernel hotfix at ~10:20 that removed the slow code path.
- Rebalanced model shards and cleared the KV eviction queue; monitored token pacing across the pool.
- Enabled an emergency routing policy to divert new streaming sessions away from the impacted pool until 12:00 EST.

4) Customer-facing mitigations (what you can do now)
- Where acceptable, switch to non-streaming (single response) for high-availability flows.
- Reduce max_tokens to 256 for interactive sessions to shorten the chance window.
- Implement the client-side gap-detection + retry pattern we described (initial timeout 250ms, exponential backoff).
- If you rely on partial updates, enable a parallel polling path for critical UI updates.

5) Financial & next steps
- We've proposed a goodwill credit equal to 5% of November usage for impacted API calls while we close the postmortem with your team. Ben has drafts ready and will finalize after we confirm your impacted volume.
- Marissa will share a short formal postmortem PDF and a link to the runbook we used for mitigation: https://drive.google.com/open?id=example-postmortem (attached).
- We've filed JIRA-QS-4872 with the telemetry and remediation actions.

Apology: I’m sorry for the disruption to your customers — we know latency on streaming endpoints can have an outsized product impact. We appreciate your partnership and the quick trace you provided; that sped up the investigation considerably.

If you'd like a short sync to review the postmortem and the runbook, Marissa and I are available this afternoon.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
